documents.reason: The closed-hall corridor risk still motivates advertising staffed hours and the drop-off location. Reused box designs still motivate copying the manufacturer's title and count, while the characters-versus-sky example explains why contributors can also describe challenging sections. Only playable incomplete puzzles are grouped, and takers still judge the known gap from a removable note. Volunteers still seal loose pieces before shelving. Actual size and sample outlines support people with limited grip, reachable bottom shelves are reserved for children's boxes with original age guidance, and a clean donor image substitutes when a damaged lid needs one. The donor still takes back boxes showing moisture or mildew after inspection in good light. Accepted-box identifiers still let residents report issues without recalling the title or describing the art, help staff match found pieces kept in labeled envelopes behind the desk, and help neighbors locate the puzzle pictured in a builder's noticeboard photo.
